senses.gloss: m. (שָׂרַף I) acrid substance, esp. vegetable sap made thick by inspissation; resin, gum (secreted by the heat of the sun).
units: <cite ref="Berakhot 44a:7">Ber. 44ᵃ</cite> <he>כל סעודה שאין בה ש׳ וכ׳</he> Ms. M. (ed. <cite ref="U01980"><he>שָׂרִיף</he></cite>) a meal without an acrid substance (bitter herbs &c.) is no meal.

<cite ref="Tosefta Pesachim 1:33">Tosef. ib. I</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Pesachim 2:33">II</cite>), 33 <he>כל שיש בו ש׳ וכ׳</he> any plant which contains an acrid sap is fit to be used on the Passover night.

<cite ref="Mishnah Orlah 1:7">Orl. I, 7</cite> <he>שְׂרַף העלים</he> the sap of leaves; <he>ש׳ העקרים</he> of roots; <he>ש׳ הפגים</he> of unripe grapes. Y. ib. I, 61ᵇ bot. <he>למה ש׳ פרי פגין פרי</he> why (this difference in the law between resin and juice of unripe fruits)? resin is fruit and grapes are fruit. Ib. <he>קטף בטל ע״י שִׂרְפּוֹ</he> resin ceases to exist when its sap is pressed out; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 7:2:6">Y. Shebi. VII, end, 37ᶜ</cite>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 7:2:6">Ib.</cite> <he>אילן אינו בטל ע״ג שרפו</he> the tree does not cease to exist when its sap is tapped.

<cite ref="Keritot 6a:51">Ker. 6ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Shabbat 26a:6">Sabb. 26ᵃ</cite> <he>צרי אינו אלא ש׳ וכ׳</he> balsam is only a gum that drips from the balsam tree. Y. ib. II, 4ᵈ <he>אין … מפני שהוא ש׳</he> you must not use balsam for the Sabbath light, because it is a gum.
Gen. R. s. 94, v. סָפַג; Tanḥ. B’midbar 16 השבט (corr. acc.); a. e.—Trnsf. secretion, matter.

<cite ref="Niddah 10b:4">Nidd. 10ᵇ</cite> <he>זו שִׂירְפָּה מצוי וכ׳</he> with the one (the newly married virgin) secretion (from a wound caused by first coition) is frequent &c.; [oth. opin.: with the wife of older standing secretion is frequent].—Pl. <he>שְׂרָפִים</he>, <he>שְׂרָפִין</he>.
<cite ref="Shabbat 23a:5">Sabb. 23ᵃ</cite> <he>כל הש׳ יפין וכ׳</he> all gums are good for ink, but the gum of the balsam tree is the best.
